description.narrative: The development objective of the Payments System Project is to improve Guyana's national payments system by enhancing safety and efficiency of payments. It has three main components. The first component, developing payments system infrastructure will focus on financing the required hardware and software infrastructure by the Government in order to provide interbank clearing and settlement services for electronic payments. The component will finance the hardware and software for the Real-Time Gross Settlement System (RTGS) to be operated by the Bank of Guyana (BoG). The component will finance the hardware and software for the Central Securities Depository (CSD) to be operated by the Bank of Guyana. The project will also finance an information security audit of the payments systems technical infrastructure and will finance activities to promote the engagement of the private sector's usage of electronic payments. The second component, Capacity Building of the BoG is mainly focusing on the capacity building of BoG staff in the specific technical areas required for ongoing operation and management of the infrastructure systems. This project brings together multiple Information and Communication Technology (ICT) activities and would hence require the support of consultants and entities that would assist the new Project Implementation Unit (PIU) in managing the implementation aspects of the ICT activities. Completion of relevant training and study tours would also further strengthen the capacity of the relevant Bank of Guyana staff and would be financed under this component. The third component, project implementation unit will focus on supporting the efforts of the implementing agency to effectively execute the Payments System Project.
The project development objective is to improve Guyana's national payments system by enhancing safety and efficiency of payments.

title.narrative: Percentage of large-value payments processed through the RTGS (Turnover of GDP)

comment.narrative:
<p>The Project achieved this PDO indicator. </p>

<p><strong>14.98 percent of large-value payments were processed throughthe RTGS (Turnover of GDP).</strong> To estimate the target achieved at completion (the amount equivalent to the value the GDP settled in a year by the RTGS), it was considered the annual amount of transactions processed from April 2021 to March 2022 (from the following month after the RTGS became operative). In that period, 2,857 large-value transactions were processed by commercial banks through the RTGS, about US$1.11 billion (GY$232 billion), which represented 14.98 percent of large-value payments processed through the RTGS (Turnover of GDP). </p>

<p>As of May 31, 2022 (Closing Date), 3,602 large-valuetransactions (> US$25,000) were processed by commercial banks through the RTGS since the system became operative on March 11, 2021, about US$1.77 billion (GY$370 billion). After the project closed, as of September 30, 2020, the total amount of transactions was 4,974, about US$2.48 billion (GY$519 billion). </p>

<p>The Project achieved both the original target and the formally revised target. The original target was 12 percent annually, in line with the average annual value of RTGS payments processed among countries with similar economic characteristics as Guyana, ranging 10-12 percent, (even though it showed as 120 percent in the PAD, due to a portal glitch at the beginning which misreflected the actual figure). The target was revised from 12 to 7percent in the restructure of February 2021 to better reflect the results of 9 months using the system instead of 12 months since the project would have closed on December 31, 2021. After that, the project was extended twice until May 31, 2022; therefore, it was possible to calculate the indicator in an annual basis. </p>

<p>The numbers reflected in this indicators are considering only transactions processed by the commercial banks operating in Guyana. MoF is expected to start processing transactions through the RTGS the second quarter of 2023  and GRA is projecting start using the RTGS by the end of 2022.</p>

title.narrative: National Insurance Scheme is connected to the RTGS and ACH platform

comment.narrative:
<p>The National Insurance Scheme is connected to the Electronic Fund Transfer System - Part of the ACH; however, it has not started processing payments through the EFT yet.</p>
<p>This indicator was revised during the restructuring on September 2021 toclarify that National Insurance Scheme will be connected only to the ACH Platform since the institution manages small payments and not large-value payments to be processed through the RTGS. (This adjustment is not reflected due to a portal issue). </p>
